span.p:
Do third-party apps need access
to your users' data?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Use OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow + PKCE

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Multiple independent frontends
sharing a single backend?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Consider OAuth2 if you plan
to open to third parties later

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Internal microservices
with a service mesh?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Use mTLS with SPIFFE identities
No OAuth2 needed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Use session cookies or API keys
(simple, no OAuth2 overhead)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Rule of thumb: Third-party delegation -> OAuth2.
User-facing first-party app -> Session cookies. Service-to-service -> mTLS.
CLI/automation -> API key. Read-only public data -> No auth.
